Escalation from the fulfillment team — two complaints that they swear started together, and both reproduce on a clean checkout: `go test -race -timeout 120s ./...` covers them.

1. Stock listings go strange right after someone opens the availability dashboard. GET /warehouses/{id}/stock normally comes back ordered by SKU; the moment anyone pulls that warehouse's report, the listing comes back in a different order — and the next restock of a SKU we already carry shows up as a SECOND row for that SKU instead of topping up the existing one, so the on-hand count is split across two rows from then on. Reconciliation then flags mismatches on that warehouse even though every single movement went through the API; nothing happened off the books.

2. Any night the floor team runs a counting session (lock, count, unlock), the reconciliation ledger goes bad afterwards. The job correctly waits out the count and retries a little later — but from the next night on there are TWO ledger entries per night, roughly fifteen minutes apart, and it never settles back to one per night.

Please work out what's actually happening and fix it. stockroom_test.go is the acceptance bar and is read-only.

TASK
Ticket for the analytics sprint: the editor dashboard is getting a "top words" widget and the wordfreq package needs to grow two things to back it.

1) TopK(k) on Counter, returning a []Entry (word + count) of the k most frequent words, most frequent first. Ties MUST break alphabetically — the widget snapshots its output and diffs it between runs, so map-order randomness leaking into the result is an instant bug report. k bigger than the vocabulary just returns everything; k <= 0 returns nothing.

2) Stopword filtering, but at REPORT time, not ingest time. SetStopwords takes a list; those words disappear from TopK output (the next-ranked words fill the slots) but the raw tally — Count, Total, Distinct — must not change, because the same Counter also feeds the vocabulary-size job. Matching is case-insensitive, and each SetStopwords call replaces the previous set outright (passing nil clears it), it does not merge.

topk_test.go is the acceptance contract for all of this. wordfreq_test.go pins today's tokenizing/counting behavior and every bit of it has to keep passing — don't touch either test file. go test -race -timeout 30s ./... is the check.

export an async generator splitLines(chunks) where chunks is an AsyncIterable<string> or a plain Iterable<string>, yielding one complete line at a time with the terminator removed.

Empty chunks can appear anywhere and mean nothing. And it must actually stream — emit each line as soon as its chunk has arrived, don't slurp the whole source (we tail files that never end).

state:
TASK
CI build queue, the cancel-on-archive path. When a repo gets archived we cancel everything it has queued, but runners keep picking up builds for repos that no longer exist. It's maddeningly inconsistent: sometimes one cancel clears the repo completely, sometimes a chunk of its builds survive. The day we archived the monorepo mirror — its builds were most of the queue — more of its jobs survived the purge than got cancelled, and the cancelled-count we wrote to the audit log was short by exactly the number of survivors. Support has even found a 'workaround': pressing cancel a second time usually mops up the stragglers, which tells me the queue data itself is fine. For what it's worth, cancel_branch (the force-push cleanup) has never misbehaved. Queue order is explicitly not a promise — runners select by build id — but membership and the returned counts have to be exact: one cancel_repo call removes every queued build for that repo, returns how many it removed, and a second call finds nothing. `cargo test --offline` reproduces all of it. Fix src/lib.rs and leave tests/, Cargo.toml, and .gitignore alone.

Ops ticket from Ledgerline billing, priority high. Tuesday morning a customer statement went out stamped DRAFT. The stamp was added hours earlier by a one-off staging re-run somebody kicked off through the review UI — different document, different job, but the customer's export picked it up anyway. Please find and fix the actual root cause — don't paper over it by capping retries harder or special-casing status codes inside the importer loop.

- now(): current virtual ms, starts at 0

- scheduleRepeating(fn, intervalMs): fire

vance target; tasks a callback schedules during the advance also run if they land inside the window; afterwards now() is the advance target

Both symptoms have to go away — fix src/lib.rs, don't touch tests/, Cargo.toml, or .gitignore.

The nightly receiving summary has been reporting zero work for three nights running, and the depot leads are (rightly) asking why the dashboard says nobody scanned anything. The maddening part: the report prints its per-item lines just fine and then contradicts itself two lines later. Run it yourself:

    bash nightly_report.sh sample.log

and you get

    handled AA-1042 x3
    handled BB-77 x12
    handled AA-9 x1
    handled DD-3 x5
    handled BB-77 x2
    -- nightly totals --
    scans: 0
    items: 0
    depots:

Five handled lines directly above, then scans: 0, items: 0, and the depots section is completely empty. My first guess was that our filter pattern was somehow dropping the scan lines before they got counted, but obviously not — the handled lines are RIGHT THERE, printed by the same loop that does the counting. I've stared at the arithmetic and it looks textbook.

Please fix nightly_report.sh so the totals block agrees with the handled lines: scans should count them, items should sum the quantities, and the depots section should show the per-depot item sums. Don't change the report format, the handled lines, or the skipped-line warnings — downstream tooling scrapes all of it. `bash test_lostcount.sh` is the regression gate; it must pass unmodified, and leave the test file alone.

...[TRUNCATED 2027 CHARS]...
 byte-for-byte unchanged. Reparenting to the parent it already has is legal and moves it to the BACK of the child list. Reparenting a detached node is a plain attach. Subtrees ride along whole.

Our county birding club runs a little merge tool for the weekly sighting roundup — spotters send in reports, and the log is supposed to collapse duplicate reports of the same sighting (same species code, same site, same date; the spotter is just attribution). This week's newsletter listed the same pileated woodpecker at Cedar Bog THREE times because three members reported it, the "already recorded?" check answers no for sightings that are definitely in the log, and every "confirmed by N observers" tally shows 1 or 0. So the comparison rules seem right, and yet the log behaves as if every report is brand new.

Repro is `java TestMain.java` (plain JDK, source launcher, no build step) — it feeds a known week of reports through and checks the roundup numbers. Find whatever is actually wrong, fix it, and get the suite green. Do not touch TestMain.java.

The log shipper is shipping garbage and I'm losing my mind. Receiver-side we see two flavors of nonsense: most batches bounce with `wire: corrupt frame: declared payload 34 bytes, frame carries 63` style errors, and the batches that DO land decode as the same record repeated — always whatever was logged LAST in that interval, so the invoice audit log for Tuesday is 4000 copies of 'retrying webhook'. It gets better: when an upload fails and the shipper retries the batch after new traffic has come in, the retried batch arrives containing the NEW records, not the ones that failed. Encode-one-decode-one in isolation is spotless, CRCs and all, which is why this sat unnoticed until finance diffed the audit log. Everything lives in wire.go (encoder, batch, decoder). wire_test.go now reproduces all of it — leave the tests alone, find what's actually wrong and fix it, then show me `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...` green.
